before: A pseudo-element styles a generated part of an element. ::before creates a box before its contents when content supplies a value. Here an empty string creates a decorative shape; the actual message stays in HTML.

The two colons distinguish a pseudo-element from a state pseudo-class. content: "" supplies no words but still permits the box; content: none suppresses it. display: inline-block allows the marker to have width and height while sitting with text. Do not put essential instructions only in generated content: availability to assistive technology varies.

after: A pseudo-element is a page part made or selected by CSS. `::before` can add a box before an element’s content. The two colons mark it as a pseudo-element.
`content: ""` creates the box without adding words. `content: none` means the box is not created. `display: inline-block` lets the box have a width and height while sitting beside text.

before.question: If content changes to none while width stays 8px, what happens to the decorative box?
choices: It becomes an 8px empty word in the HTML.
It moves after the paragraph automatically.
before.explanation: The content setting controls whether the pseudo-element is generated. Width alone does not create it.

after.question: You change content to none but keep width at 8px. What happens to the marker?
choices: It becomes an empty word in the HTML.
after.explanation: Width sets the size of a box; it does not create the box when content is none.
